article.title: 阅读一 · 外部董事为何提前离场
article.context: 公司治理与外部董事的声誉激励。朗读保持分析感，数据处清晰克制。
rows: Ruth Simmons joined Goldman Sachs’s board as an outside director in January 2000; a year later she became president of Brown University.|For the rest of the decade she apparently managed both roles without attracting much criticism.|But by the end of 2009 Ms. Simmons was under fire for having sat on Goldman’s compensation committee; how could she have let those enormous bonus payouts pass unremarked?|By February the next year Ms. Simmons had left the board.|The position was just taking up too much time, she said.|Outside directors are supposed to serve as helpful, yet less biased, advisers on a firm’s board.|Having made their wealth and their reputations elsewhere, they presumably have enough independence to disagree with the chief executive’s proposals.|If the sky, and the share price is falling, outside directors should be able to give advice based on having weathered their own crises.|The researchers from Ohio University used a database that covered more than 10,000 firms and more than 64,000 different directors between 1989 and 2004.|Then they simply checked which directors stayed from one proxy statement to the next.|The most likely reason for departing a board was age, so the researchers concentrated on those “surprise” disappearances by directors under the age of 70.|They found that after a surprise departure, the probability that the company will subsequently have to restate earnings increases by nearly 20%.|The likelihood of being named in a federal class-action lawsuit also increases, and the stock is likely to perform worse.|The effect tended to be larger for larger firms.|Although a correlation between them leaving and subsequent bad performance at the firm is suggestive, it does not mean that such directors are always jumping off a sinking ship.|Often they “trade up,” leaving riskier, smaller firms for larger and more stable firms.|But the researchers believe that outside directors have an easier time of avoiding a blow to their reputations if they leave a firm before bad news breaks, even if a review of history shows they were on the board at the time any wrongdoing occurred.|Firms who want to keep their outside directors through tough times may have to create incentives.|Otherwise outside directors will follow the example of Ms. Simmons, once again very popular on campus.

露丝·西蒙斯2000年1月以外部董事身份加入高盛董事会，一年后出任布朗大学校长。在此后的大部分时间里，她似乎同时兼顾两个职位，并未招致多少批评。但到2009年底，她因曾担任高盛薪酬委员会成员而受到抨击：那些巨额奖金发放，她怎么会听之任之、毫无异议？第二年2月，她离开了董事会，并称这个职位占用了太多时间。外部董事本应在公司董事会中充当有帮助、同时相对不偏不倚的顾问。他们的财富和声誉通常来自别处，理论上应有足够独立性去反对首席执行官的提议。当形势恶化、股价下跌时，他们也应凭借自己曾渡过危机的经验提出建议。俄亥俄大学的研究人员利用一个数据库，研究了1989至2004年间一万多家公司、六万四千多名董事，并简单核查哪些董事会成员会从一份委托书持续留任到下一份。离开董事会最常见的原因是年龄，因此研究人员把注意力集中在70岁以下董事“意外”离任的情况上。他们发现，董事意外离任后，公司随后重述财务收益的概率上升近20%；公司被列入联邦集体诉讼的可能性也会上升，股票表现也往往更差，而且大型公司中的这种效应更明显。虽然董事离任与公司之后表现不佳之间存在相关性，但这并不意味着他们总是在“跳离沉船”。很多时候，他们是在“向上换位”：离开风险较高的小公司，转去规模更大、更稳定的公司。不过研究人员认为，如果外部董事能在坏消息爆发之前离开公司，就更容易避免自己的声誉受损，即使事后回顾发现，他们在违规行为发生时其实已经身处董事会。那些希望外部董事在困难时期仍留下来的公司，也许必须设计相应激励；否则，外部董事就可能效仿西蒙斯——重新成为校园里颇受欢迎的人物。
